0.title: Interactive Sync Review & Deletion Diff Visualizer
0.content: Standard automated sync daemons run unattended in background crons. When an unexpected deletion wave occurs—such as an operator accidentally moving a root directory or an external service wiping a folder—unattended sync immediately replicates the wipe across all replicas. Bisync Hub introduces an interactive human-in-the-loop inspection barrier before destructive mutations are committed.

1.title: How It Works
1.content: [ Trigger Sync ] ──► [ Dry-Run Operation ] ──► [ Parse Mutation List ] │ ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ Deletions <= Max Threshold Deletions > Max Threshold │ │ ▼ ▼ [ Auto-Apply Policies ] [ HALT & Emit Review Event ] │ ▼ [ Operator Decision Modal ] • Confirm Specific Deletes • Reject / Abort Run • Override Heuristics .

2.title: 1. Dry-Run Mutation Analysis
2.content: Every scheduled or manual sync cycle executes in --dry-run inspection mode first. The engine streams the stdout/stderr mutation log and categorizes every proposed operation: . | + CREATE: New file appearing on either Path1 or Path2. | ~ MODIFY: Content or metadata discrepancy requiring replication. | - DELETE: Proposed removal of a file or directory. | .

3.title: 2. High-Severity Quota Halts
3.content: If proposed deletions exceed either: . | The absolute file limit (e.g. MAX_DELETE_COUNT=50), or | The directory percentage ratio (e.g. MAX_DELETE_PERCENT=10%), | . the sync engine immediately trips the circuit breaker, writes an atomic .review_pending state, and emits real-time WebSocket notifications to the management dashboard.

4.title: 3. Granular Operator Triage
4.content: Operators can open the Web Dashboard review modal to: . | Inspect file diffs, file sizes, and last modified timestamps side-by-side. | View intelligent heuristic evaluations (e.g. temporary lock file detection, canary protection, user local deletion identification). | Selectively confirm specific deletions, restore/reject items, or auto-apply heuristic recommendations in batch. | Stage atomic pre-mutation backups and trigger an authorized force sync directly from the modal. | . Safety Guarantee: No file is ever removed when a review threshold is tripped until an authorized operator explicitly signs off or an automated timeout policy executes an abort.

6.title: 1. Barrier Activation on Threshold Exceeded
6.content: When deletion or conflict limits are breached during pre-flight analysis, the engine disengages automated replication and displays the persistent review barrier banner in the dashboard cockpit: . 1. Sync Review Barrier Engaged Automated sync halted; operator intervention required

11.title: Multi-Analyzer Heuristic Conflict Engine
11.content: Most bidirectional sync tools rely on a naive, binary rule: “newer timestamp wins”. In distributed cloud environments, this rule causes silent data loss because: . | Cloud storage APIs (e.g. Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint) round timestamps to 1-second or 2-second windows or update them asynchronously. | Device clocks can drift or suffer skew during daylight savings transitions. | Rapid concurrent edits on mobile and desktop produce collisions where the “newer” file is actually an incomplete draft. | . Bisync Hub replaces timestamp gambling with a multi-analyzer heuristic confidence engine.

12.title: The Evaluation Pipeline
12.content: When both Path1 and Path2 report modifications to the same file path, the engine executes four independent heuristic analyzers: . | Heuristic Analyzer | Signal Analyzed | Weight | Description | . | SizeDivergenceAnalyzer | Content volume delta | 30% | Detects dramatic file shrinks or expansions indicating truncation or major additions. | . | BinarySignatureAnalyzer | MIME & header magic bytes | 25% | Verifies format validity (e.g. SQLite database header, JPEG signatures) to penalize corrupt partial writes. | . | ClockSkewAnalyzer | Cross-remote timestamp drift | 25% | Evaluates cloud API timestamp granularity and compensates for known provider skews (e.g., OneDrive 2s window). | . | VelocityAnalyzer | Modification frequency | 20% | Scores edit frequency to distinguish steady active editing from stale background touches. | .

13.title: Confidence Calculation & Safety Bands
13.content: The engine aggregates individual analyzer scores into a unified Confidence Index (0% - 100%): . Score >= 85% ──► [ HIGH CONFIDENCE ] ──► Auto-resolve in favor of dominant replica 60% - 84% ──► [ MEDIUM CONFIDENCE ]──► Backup losing candidate to .conflict-bak, then sync Score < 60% ──► [ LOW CONFIDENCE ] ──► QUARANTINE: Halt file mutation & prompt Operator .

14.title: Safety Features
14.content: . | Deterministic Quarantine: Unresolvable collisions are safely preserved in a .bisync_quarantine/ isolation jail. | Conflict Backup Preserves: Even on high-confidence resolutions, the displaced version is moved to the backup store before overwriting. | Clock Skew Tolerance: Built-in compensation algorithms for cloud timestamp drift and DST shifts. | . All heuristic scoring weights and confidence thresholds are fully configurable in bisync.env to match your organization’s risk tolerance.

16.title: Customizable Safety Policies & Circuit Breakers
16.content: ● Shipped & Active . Core Safety Tenets: Pre-execution canary protection (RCLONE_TEST), path confinement filesystem jails, and pre-mutation deletion quotas (SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT, SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO) are fully active in the core engine. Dynamic in-dashboard parameter configuration is scheduled for the upcoming Configuration & Setup Manager milestone. Automated tools must know when to stop. Running bidirectional synchronization when a network share is unmounted, when a cloud provider returns HTTP 429 rate limits, or when a disk is failing will corrupt sync state and trigger cascading deletions. Bisync Hub implements a two-stage defensive policy barrier: Pre-Execution and Pre-Mutation.

18.title: 1. Pre-Execution Validation Gates
18.content: Before invoking any sync or check command, Bisync Hub checks environmental invariants: . | Canary File Verification (RCLONE_TEST): . | Requires a known marker file to exist on both local and remote mount roots. | If a network volume unmounts or cloud sync token expires, the canary file disappears. The engine detects this and aborts instantly, preventing the empty directory from being treated as a mass deletion. | . | Path Confinement (Filesystem Jail): . | All local file manipulations are strictly validated with filepath.Rel and prefix checks to ensure zero path traversal escapes outside designated sync roots. | . | Advisory POSIX Locking (flock): . | Prevents overlapping sync jobs from corrupting local metadata or triggering race conditions across systemd timers or manual CLI runs. | . | .

19.title: 2. Pre-Mutation Circuit Breakers
19.content: During sync execution, incoming mutation requests pass through configurable circuit breakers: . # bisync.env safety settings SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_COUNT=25 # Hard limit on total file removals per run SAFETY_MAX_DELETE_RATIO=0.10 # Maximum 10% of total files may be deleted SAFETY_ENABLE_CANARY=true # Canary file mandatory on both remotes SAFETY_RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF=true # Exponential backoff on provider HTTP 429 .

20.title: 3. Automatic Backoff & Quarantine
20.content: . | Provider Throttling: When Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive signals rate limits (429 Too Many Requests), Bisync Hub immediately halts further calls and enforces exponential backoff with jitter. | Fail-Safe Abort: Any violation of a safety policy halts execution cleanly and logs the event to the audit ledger. | . Zero Canary Bypass Policy: Canary check routines are hardcoded to fail-closed. If canary status is ambiguous, sync execution is blocked.

22.title: Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger
22.content: ● Shipped & Available . Production Ledger: The Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger is fully implemented and included in the native binary. Every synchronization action, conflict resolution, and file mutation is cryptographically sealed into an append-only SQLite database backed by SHA-256 hash chains. Compliance, security audits, and forensic debugging require an undeniable, tamper-evident record of all storage mutations: Who deleted file X? When was conflict Y resolved? What was the decision confidence score? . Bisync Hub embeds an immutable, SQLite-backed cryptographic ledger with trigger-enforced append-only constraints.

24.title: 1. SQLite Trigger-Enforced Immutability
24.content: The internal SQLite database employs schema-level BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers on audit tables: . CREATE TRIGGER prevent_ledger_tampering BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_events BEGIN SELECT RAISE(FAIL, 'FATAL: audit_events table is strictly append-only.'); END; . Even if an attacker or misconfigured script gains write access to the database file, existing audit entries cannot be modified or purged without breaking database integrity.

25.title: 2. SHA-256 Hash Chaining
25.content: Each audit entry computes a SHA-256 digest over the concatenation of: . | Previous_Record_Hash | Event_Type and Timestamp (UTC millisecond precision) | Payload_JSON (redacted secrets, sanitized paths, decision scores) | . The application provides a built-in cryptographic verification command (bisync-hub verify-ledger) to audit chain integrity and identify any external byte tampering.

26.title: 3. Redaction by Default
26.content: All sensitive credentials—including RC_PASS, OAuth refresh tokens, webhook URLs, and private auth headers—are recursively redacted via security.RedactSecrets before entering the audit stream. The audit ledger ensures full compliance with operational standards while protecting organizational data sovereignty.

You can deploy Bisync Hub to an edge Raspberry Pi, a corporate Linux server, or a NAS box with a single scp command.

37.title: Architecture & Safety Principles
37.content: Bisync Hub is designed under the assumption that networks drop, cloud APIs produce unexpected HTTP responses, and distributed clocks drift. Every design decision adheres to three foundational tenets: . | Visibility Before Action: Never mutate remote storage silently without an immutable record and pre-flight inspection. | Safety Before Automation: If an environmental invariant is violated (e.g. missing canary, unresolvable conflict), halt immediately rather than guess. | Defense in Depth: Protect the host filesystem with path confinement jails, POSIX process flocking, and secret scrubbing. | .

39.title: 1. Filesystem Path Confinement Jails
39.content: When browsing files or preparing sync operations on local storage endpoints, Bisync Hub prevents arbitrary filesystem access by enforcing strict jail boundaries: . // Enforcing local path isolation relPath, err := filepath.Rel(jailRoot, targetPath) if err != nil || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "..") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, "/") { return ErrPathTraversalViolation } . Any request attempting directory traversal (../) outside the configured root returns an immediate authorization violation and is recorded in the audit log.

40.title: 2. POSIX Flock Process Isolation
40.content: To avoid lock races between scheduled background timers, cron jobs, and interactive operator CLI requests, Bisync Hub acquires advisory file locks using native POSIX flock(fd, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB). | Concurrent executions fail fast with a clear error rather than piling up or corrupting state. | Stale lock detection cleans up safely if a previous process terminated abnormally. | .

41.title: 3. Secret Redaction at Every Boundary
41.content: All external inputs, configuration files, and API logs pass through recursive sanitization via security.RedactSecrets. | Keywords matching PASS, TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, and CREDENTIAL are dynamically masked ([REDACTED]). | Raw tokens are never persisted in SQLite ledger records, JSON error messages, or telemetry streams. | .

42.title: 4. Zero-Exposure CI/CD Security
42.content: Bisync Hub’s GitHub Actions pipelines are deployed 100% on cloud-hosted ephemeral runners (ubuntu-latest) with zero self-hosted runner exposure. Every commit is validated with: . | Static analysis via go vet and staticcheck | Automated leak scanning via betterleaks | Vulnerability auditing via govulncheck | Strict branch protection with sole review governance (@slemmercs) | .

43.title: 5. High-Performance Go Quality Gate (cmd/check)
43.content: To catch regressions early during local development, Bisync Hub includes a dedicated native Go audit engine (cmd/check) executing check stages in parallel: . | True HTML Tokenization: Multi-line attribute tokenization preventing Alpine.js boolean attribute coercion bugs (:disabled, :readonly). | Architectural LOC Budgets: Single-pass line-count enforcement ensuring services remain modular and stay under ~400 LOC. | Coverage Assurance: Pre-commit validation enforcing >80% statement coverage across all packages (currently at 88.3%). | .

46.title: Why Not Just Run a Cron Script?
46.content: Cron scripts are ubiquitous, but they fail silently when edge cases occur: . | The Unmounted Mount Disaster: If an NFS/SMB share or rclone mount disconnects, an automated cron script sees an empty folder and issues deletions for thousands of files across the remote replica. | The Cloud Timestamp Shift: Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive report timestamps differently than local ext4/APFS filesystems. A simple script relying on test fileA -nt fileB frequently overwrites valid changes. | Overlapping Job Corruption: If a sync run takes longer than the cron interval (e.g., due to large video uploads), concurrent sync instances access the cache simultaneously, corrupting .bisync lock state. | . Bisync Hub eliminates every one of these failure modes out of the box.

84.content: . | Dry-Run Inspection Stream: Captures dry-run stdout/stderr, categorizing every action into + CREATE, ~ MODIFY, or - DELETE. | Operator Review Modal: Halts destructive execution when deletion thresholds are tripped, allowing granular per-file approval or full-run abort. | Rollback Resilience: Zero-byte hard link backups and recovery staging prevent accidental local wipes. | .

85.title: 2. Multi-Analyzer Heuristic Conflict Engine
85.content: . | 4 Parallel Heuristic Analyzers: . | SizeDivergenceAnalyzer (30% weight): Detects unexpected file truncations and major additions. | BinarySignatureAnalyzer (25% weight): Inspects MIME and magic bytes to reject corrupted partial writes. | ClockSkewAnalyzer (25% weight): Compensates for provider-specific API clock rounding (e.g. OneDrive 2-second timestamp windows and DST shifts). | VelocityAnalyzer (20% weight): Evaluates modification frequency to differentiate active work from background touches. | . | Graduated Confidence Bands: Automatically commits resolutions scoring $\ge 85\%$, stages backups for $60\% - 84\%$, and safely quarantines $< 60\%$ collisions for manual operator review. | .

86.title: 3. Cryptographic Immutable Audit Ledger
86.content: . | Append-Only SQLite Storage: Schema-level BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers prevent modifying or purging existing ledger entries. | SHA-256 Cryptographic Hash Chaining: Links each block to its predecessor (H_n = SHA256(H_{n-1} || payload || timestamp)), ensuring forensic tamper evidence. | In-Process POSIX Log Rotator: Thread-safe size-bounded rotation (bisync.log) with lazy initialization and dual-stream audit logging ("type": "audit"). | Interactive Audit Explorer: Dedicated Web UI tab with live cryptographic chain verification, actor/action filtering, and CSV/JSONL compliance export. | Recursive Secret Sanitization: Deep masking (security.RedactSecrets) strips all tokens, secrets, and auth headers before persistence. | .

87.title: 4. Production Go Architecture & Embedded UI
87.content: . | Single Binary Artifact: Pure Go binary with embedded dashboard assets (go:embed). No Node.js, Python, or external runtime required. | Advisory POSIX Locking: Race-free process exclusion via syscall.Flock ensures zero metadata collisions between background daemons and interactive CLI invocations. | Path Confinement Jails: Directory traversal (../) prevention protects local storage roots. | Rclone Integration: Seamless inter-process communication with Rclone RC API and local filesystem synchronization. | .

88.title: 5. High-Performance Go Quality Engine (cmd/check) & E2E Testing
88.content: . | Parallel Quality Gate: Concurrent Go CLI check runner validating formatting, templates, line-count budgets, linters, and tests in under 10 seconds. | Multi-Line HTML Attribute Tokenizer: True AST-style token parsing ignoring comments and detecting dotted boolean attributes (:disabled, :readonly). | Headless Chrome E2E Suite: Smoke tests using chromedp executing against the live embedded dashboard to verify real browser DOM reactivity. | Coverage Assurance: Statement coverage actively verified at 88.3% across all packages. | .

89.title: 6. Decoupled Service Architecture (Sub-400 LOC Enforcement)
89.content: . | Bounded Contexts: Core logic decoupled into focused domain engines (TelemetryService, CanaryService, DeletionService, ReviewService, ExplorerService, SyncService). | Strict Maintainability Limits: All Go files strictly enforced to remain under ~400 lines of code to prevent architectural drift. | .

90.title: 🟡 Near-Term Strategic Priorities (In Development)
90.content: The following capabilities represent our immediate development milestones following public launch: .

91.title: Priority 1: Multi-Profile Workspace Manager
91.content: . | Objective: Manage multiple independent synchronization pairs from a single daemon and dashboard. | Architecture: . | Spawns isolated goroutine runners per profile (e.g. Personal Google Drive, Work OneDrive, NAS backup). | Pairs independent local folders to different cloud remotes with dedicated POSIX flock isolation (/tmp/rclone-bisync-<profile>.lock). | Profile-aware telemetry streams, speed charts, and file explorer remote routing. | Refer to Multi-Profile Design Specification. | . | .

92.title: Priority 2: In-Dashboard Configuration & Setup Manager
92.content: . | Objective: Provide safe visual editing of sync flags, intervals, and remote setup. | Architecture: . | Visual Flag Editor: Adjust --buffer-size, --tpslimit, conflict strategies, and webhook endpoints safely from the UI. | Setup & Onboarding Wizard: Guided visual setup wizard for initial Rclone RC remote pairing and environment configuration. | 3-Layer Safety Pipeline: Automated backup snapshots, SHA-256 integrity match, and schema validation before applying changes. | One-Click Rollback API: Restore historical configurations immediately if a change fails verification. | . | .

93.title: Priority 3: In-App User Guidance & Diagnostic Manual
93.content: . | Objective: Enhance operational clarity and assisted recovery directly within the UI. | Architecture: . | Contextual Tooltips & Policy Explanations: Inline tooltips and modal banners explaining safety triggers (TOO_MANY_DELETES, MANDATORY_SUBDIR, heuristic risk scores) in plain language. | In-Dashboard Reference Manual: A dedicated slide-over panel summarizing CLI commands, Rclone flags, and step-by-step conflict recovery workflows. | Interactive Diagnostics: Integrated troubleshooting guides for resolving OAuth token drops, path permissions issues, and systemd service status. | . | .

94.title: Priority 4: Remote Mount Lifecycle Manager & Storage Pooling (internal/mount)
94.content: . | Objective: Turn fragile OS FUSE mounts into resilient, self-healing virtual storage endpoints. | Architecture: . | Stage A (Remote Mount Manager): Pure-Go daemon managing rclone mount subprocess lifecycles on Linux (FUSE) and Windows (WinFsp) with keepalive probes and clean unmount handlers (fusermount -u). | Stage B (Pooled Storage Engine): Provision stacked multi-cloud topologies (union + chunker + crypt) over RC /config/create. | Refer to Remote Mount Manager Design Specification. | . | .
